summary: Barbour County tower built by the Alabama Forestry Commission in 1941; the register says it was sold around 2020, is privately owned, and it says the tower cannot be reached by Kennedy Tower Road.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor MC-39 steel tower with 7x7-foot cab
facts.agency: Private owner; built by the Alabama Forestry Commission (per register)

access.note: Privately owned per register; the register says the tower cannot be reached by Kennedy Tower Road, where a gate stands in front of the last house on the road

events.note: Built by the Alabama Forestry Commission after a 1940 request from the Barbour County Board of Revenue
Visit report of May 1, 2019 by Andrew Zerbe calls it a usual vandalized tower and records it as not staffed
Sold by the state in a surplus auction around early 2020, per register; not corroborated by another source
Registered January 7, 2009; nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

notes_for_editor: Nearly every fact comes from the NHLR page, including the 2019 condition and staffing answers and the early-2020 sale. The sale is not corroborated; Alabama Forestry Commission or ADECA surplus auction records would settle it. The 'Staffed?' quote is the question label; the answer 'No' sits on the next line of the register. TopoQuest lists a 'Kennedy Lookout Tower' in Barbour County at N31.941825 W85.451608, 688 ft MSL (https://www.topoquest.com/place-detail.php?id=163350). Its point is about 30 m from the register's coordinates; its 688 ft differs from the register's 680 ft (207 m). Not used in the story. Height 30.5 m is converted from the 100 ft overall height; cab floor height is not given. The register's 2019 visit comments include directions to climb a right of way to the tower; deliberately not repeated, since the tower is privately owned. Two web searches found nothing else about this tower.
